newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vol ticks up, puts dominate trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vol ticks up, puts dominate trade.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options on LIFFE was steady at slightly higher levels on Monday as put trade dominated activity on the exchange, traders said.
"People are looking to buy for protection," said one salesman at a European bank. "We've got a relatively heavy data week ahead in the U.S. and also the German IFO survey on Friday."
Traders said August mid-price Bund volatility was around 4.50 percent, up from 4.20 percent at Friday's close but steady from Monday's opening levels. The August series is due to expire on July 24.
"The vol is more or less unchanged from the open but up around 30 ticks from Friday," said the salesman. "And it's been trading on the put side."
He said the biggest volume was in the 102.50 strike August puts which traded at 4.85 percent vol. By 1015 GMT, more than 4,200 lots of the 102.50 strike puts had been traded.
In addition, a healthy 4,700 lots of the 102.00 September puts had been traded and around 1,400 lots of the 101.50 put.
The underlying September Bund future was down 27 basis points on LIFFE at 102.72, off an earlier high of 103.14, just one basis point shy of the contract high.
Key retail sales data in the U.S. on Tuesday, inflation data on Wednesday and the German IFO survey of west and east German business climate indices due on Friday was keeping the market jittery.
One trader at a major British brokerage said the Bund options pits had hardly stirred on the back of the sinking mark which hit multi-year lows versus the dollar, yen and sterling on Monday.
"It hasn't even caused a ripple in the Bund pit," he said. "Things have been ticking over gently. It hasn't been a hectic morning, but there's been good volume, particularly in September puts."
